facts.claim: AuthState stores status plus user {userId,email}; initial state is unknown with no user.
The auth slice has two actions: sessionVerified sets authenticated and user; loggedOut sets unauthenticated and clears user.
The slice exports no selectors. useAuth selects state.auth inline and derives four boolean/status fields.
Login stores email from the login response through sessionVerified, then navigates to the next path.
Register ignores its register response, then logs in with the same credentials and stores the login response.
App bootstrap stores email from GET /v1/auth/me. No refresh endpoint or refresh flow exists in auth.api.ts.
No access or refresh token is stored. The backend response contract has no token field and identifies the session as the application cookie.
authApi defines xsrf and me queries plus register, login, and logout mutations. Hooks exported are useXsrfQuery, useMeQuery, lazy variants, and the three mutation hooks.
The logout mutation is an undefined-result POST to /v1/auth/logout and invalidates only the Auth tag. No endpoint side-effect callbacks appear in the file.
Requests use the session cookie via credentials include. Mutation requests copy __Host-Xsrf-Request into X-XSRF-TOKEN; no bearer token is read or attached.
The wrapper lazily seeds XSRF before a mutation when the readable cookie is absent, then performs the requested mutation.
A 401 dispatches loggedOut. There is no mutex, refresh, or retry loop; 401 is treated as a gone session.
Backend logout is POST /api/v1/auth/logout, requires CookieOrBearer authorization and antiforgery, calls SignOutAsync, reissues antiforgery tokens, and returns 204.
CookieOrBearer accepts either the Identity application cookie or a JWT bearer token. The SPA need not send an Authorization header when its cookie is valid.
facts.quote: Accepts either the ASP.NET Core Identity application cookie

facts.claim: The session cookie is __Host-RunCoach, HttpOnly, and documented as expired on logout. No refresh-token revocation call exists in Logout.
The shared API object is apiSlice with reducerPath api and six tag types. The app store includes its reducer and middleware and calls setupListeners.
@reduxjs/toolkit is declared as ^2.12.0 and installed as 2.12.0. The installed API exposes api.util.resetApiState(), documented to remove cache entries and mark queries uninitialized.
No current frontend caller of resetApiState was observed. The only useLogoutMutation occurrence is its export from auth.api.ts, with no consumer call site.
BroadcastChannel uses channel auth and the exact string message logout. The poster creates, posts, and closes a channel; subscribers match that string and return cleanup.
The existing receiver hook dispatches only loggedOut. It does not reset RTK Query state or navigate directly.
AppShell mounts both auth bootstrap and the broadcast listener. App uses the singleton store and BrowserRouter.
The route table is inline in app.component.tsx. Login and register are public; settings is inside the RequireAuth-wrapped ShellLayout route.
RequireAuth redirects unauthenticated state to /login with state.next and replace. Existing tests cover initial unauthenticated redirect and deep-link preservation.
Settings currently has Plan, Appearance, and Units only. It has no Account section, auth selector, or sign-out control.
Generated auth schemas define userId and email responses for register, login, and me, and a void logout response.
The shared test helpers provide PatchedRequest plus XSRF cookie seed and clear helpers. They do not provide a renderWithProviders helper.
base-query.spec.ts does not build a Redux store; it uses makeApi with mocked dispatch and direct base-query calls. auth.slice.spec.ts tests authReducer directly.
Component tests build small stores with configureStore and render Provider plus MemoryRouter. The guard spec is the closest store-backed pattern.
Vitest uses jsdom at https://localhost:5173/ and src/test-setup.ts. test-setup.ts only stubs ResizeObserver; it does not mock BroadcastChannel.
Frontend guidance assigns HTTP to RTK Query, global auth to Redux, and side-effect composition to custom hooks. Tests should be colocated and focus on hooks, reducers, and logic.
facts.quote: RTK Query for all HTTP interactions

risks.risk: Call resetApiState only after the logout request settles. RTK Query reset aborts all running queries and mutations.
If the receiver does not dispatch resetApiState, a second tab can retain per-user query data after it becomes unauthenticated.
A failed logout needs an explicit policy. base-query dispatches loggedOut on 401, but no existing caller performs cache reset or broadcast on mutation failure.
The logout mutation invalidates Auth only. That does not replace a full api.util.resetApiState purge for Plan, Settings, WorkoutLog, Conversation, and other tags.

result.recommendation: Add useSignOut to auth.hooks.ts. In try/finally, await logout(undefined).unwrap(), then dispatch(loggedOut()), dispatch(apiSlice.util.resetApiState()), and postLogoutBroadcast(). Update the receiver to dispatch loggedOut plus resetApiState. Wire SettingsPage to useAuth/useSignOut. Add auth.hooks.spec.ts and a live-flip test in require-auth.component.spec.tsx.
open_questions: Should local cleanup and broadcast always run in finally when logout returns 401 or 500, or only after a successful 204? The current code defines no failure policy (frontend/src/app/api/auth.api.ts:30-33; frontend/src/app/api/base-query.ts:81-85).

Should SettingsPage show a retry/error message if signOut rejects after cleanup? The current settings page has no account or auth error UI (frontend/src/app/modules/settings/pages/settings.page.tsx:19-70).

Should the second-tab receiver dispatch loggedOut before resetApiState, matching the sender sequence? The current receiver has no reset ordering to preserve (frontend/src/app/modules/auth/hooks/auth.hooks.ts:77-84).
